findings.text: follow-on: the per-item mean-rank merge is a second rank-fusion implementation beside the repository's owner rrf_fuse at imas_codex/search/fusion.py:19, which it neither extends nor cites; the two fusion definitions now drift independently. The owner's (-mass, id) tie-break cannot supply the embedding-order tie-break this change requires, but that is a reason to extend the owner (an order-preserving variant) rather than fork the capability.

follow-on: the LLMCostEvent stamps the rerank's spend with model=model, the compose model (compose_model or get_model("sn-compose")), while the rerank was billed under the sn-judge seat, so the cost row attributes the spend to the wrong model; and mgr.reserve runs only after the spend has already happened, so when it returns None under an exhausted budget the charge is silently dropped.

follow-on: rerank_name_comparators relies on rerank_pool's internal guard and omits the caller-side try/except both sibling callers use (imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:214, imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:192); a raise from get_model("sn-judge") or from a state_for builder would abort the compose batch instead of returning the embedding order, though the default-off switch limits the exposure.
